asset_test.details: Asset Test: a patient with assets exceeding 25% of household income amount may not be eligible; only assets accessible without penalty are considered.

evidence.quote: A patient with such assets that exceed 25% of such patient’s household income amount may not be eligible for financial assistance.
Patient applications can be submitted for consideration for up to 240 days past the date of service

presumptive_eligibility: Eligibility may be determined via presumptive scoring for patients with a sufficient unpaid balance and no FAP application; full adjustment FPL for presumptive assistance is set at 100% of FPL.
how_to_apply: Complete the FAP Application; phone (251) 434-3505, Mon–Fri 8 am–4:30 pm; mail USA Health, Attention: Business Office - Financial Counselor, P.O. Box 40010, Mobile, AL 36640-0010
warnings: Application window is inconsistent: the table section says 240 days past date of service, while the definition says 240 days after the first post-discharge billing statement (or 30 days after ECA notice, whichever is later); catastrophic section says 240th day after first discharge bill.
Tier boundaries overlap at 200% and 300% in the policy table (up to 200%, 200-300%, 300-400%).
Residency not explicitly required; covered providers are limited to hospitals in Mobile, Alabama and clinics in Mobile and Baldwin Counties, which is not a stated patient residency requirement.
Patients above 400% FPL may qualify via a Means Test (medical debt at or above household gross income) for the 400% FPL level of assistance (75%).
Insured patients are addressed (under-insured eligible for personally responsible portion), though out-of-network plans may reduce or deny assistance.
Financial assistance amount is described as a sliding scale; the table gives fixed percentages.
